Style: High pressing with a wing-dominant approach. The team prioritizes aggressive ball-winning, leveraging the pace of both wingers to create lethal chances, while the midfield emphasizes rapid positional rotation.

A robust defensive approach with set-pieces as the primary route to victory. Defensively, the team prioritizes physical duels, while offensively they rely on rapid progression through the midfield and dominance in aerial battles.

Compact defensive block with incisive counter-attacks. The team maintains an extremely tight shape, leveraging the mobility and outright pace of the forward line to execute a devastating counter-attacking strategy.

Relentless high pressing driven by star power. The side exhibits strict tactical discipline and exceptional physical conditioning, with their attacking output heavily reliant on the individual brilliance of overseas-based stars such as Son Heung-min and Lee Kang-in.

Adopt a deep defensive block while maintaining a potent two-wing threat. Against top-tier opposition, the team drops significantly deeper; upon regaining possession, they immediately look to launch direct counter-attacks through pacey wide players such as Alphonso Davies.

Dominant midfield control paired with a flexible defensive structure. The unit exhibits exceptional tactical discipline, boasting superior ball retention and distribution capabilities that enable seamless transitions between possession-based play and counter-attacking phases.
Target man with a physical, direct style of play. The team leverages superior physical strength to establish local dominance, relying heavily on a tall striker as the tactical focal point in attack.

Employing a back-five in a low defensive block, the team relies on a counter-attacking strategy spearheaded by a dynamic duo. The approach is built on a compact, deep defensive shape, with the attacking burden placed almost entirely on a select few highly gifted players, such as Almoez Ali (or the specific player intended by "Afif"), to unlock the opposition.

Rooted in Brazil's rich footballing heritage, the system leverages explosive wingers. While maintaining defensive solidity, it grants players like Vinícius Jr. exceptional freedom, with full-backs making frequent overlapping runs to stretch the opposition.

Iron-clad defensive organization with wing-backs acting as primary playmakers. The team drops into an exceptionally deep defensive block when out of possession, while in attack they rely heavily on the crossing and long-range distribution from left-sided wing-backs such as Robertson.

World-class defensive organization with rapid transitions. The backline is exceptionally compact and rarely makes errors, while the midfield boasts refined technical quality, enabling highly efficient counterattacks immediately upon regaining possession.

A low-block, ultra-physical approach. While the overall tactical execution is relatively crude, the squad boasts explosive athletic attributes, relying primarily on track-and-field-style sprinting to launch counter-attacks.

Premier League-style high press and extensive running coverage. Under Pochettino, the emphasis is on an intensely aggressive high press, leveraging the superior stamina of young players to drive a rapid tempo in both attack and defense.

An emotionally driven, possession-based midfield featuring technically gifted players such as Hakan Çalhanoğlu and Arda Güler. Their attacking play is flamboyant and expansive, often resulting in a match tempo that swings dramatically between high-intensity phases and open, end-to-end exchanges.

Classic English style, characterized by a direct, long-ball approach. The team maintains an exceptionally compact and disciplined defensive shape, excels in physical duels, and relies heavily on set-pieces and wide crosses to generate scoring opportunities.

A meat-grinder midfield defined by South American grit. Renowned for the "Guarani doggedness" mentality, they execute ferocious midfield interceptions and favor a direct attacking approach over ball possession.

A dual No. 10 system driving an extreme possession-and-pressing philosophy. Under Julian Nagelsmann's modern framework, the attack hinges on the diagonal runs of Jamal Musiala and Florian Wirtz into the half-spaces, while ball recovery is executed through an aggressive high press immediately after losing possession.

A squad built like an Olympic track team, specializing in vertical, direct attacks. They combine elite physical attributes with refined technical ability on the ball. Their midfield boasts exceptional ball-winning prowess (exemplified by Caicedo), immediately transitioning into vertical assaults the moment possession is regained.

A blend of physical power and explosive pace, leveraging wing-based breakthroughs. The midfield boasts significant physical dominance and progressive carrying ability, while the wingers on both flanks possess exceptional one-on-one dribbling and isolation capabilities.

A disciplined, counter-attacking approach bearing the hallmark of the Eredivisie. With a significant portion of the squad having come through Dutch youth academies, the team possesses strong tactical discipline and will resolutely execute a counter-attacking game plan against superior opposition.

A legacy of Total Football with ball-playing centre-backs. Boasting a world-class centre-back unit, the team initiates a high volume of attacks from the defensive line, while wing-backs provide essential width in the final third.

A dual-striker system built on unwavering discipline. Defensively, the unit operates with machine-like precision, while offensively, the side relies on world-class forwards such as Alexander Isak and Viktor Gyökeres to decide matches.

Asia's pinnacle of possession-based football, a pack of wolves forged in Europe. They boast exceptional midfield interplay and combination play, while their wingers—such as Kaoru Mitoma and Takefusa Kubo—possess world-class dribbling prowess at the European level.

An extreme low-block defensive setup, waiting to strike on the counter. The approach is highly conservative, specializing in disrupting the opponent's rhythm. Counter-attacks involve minimal numbers, relying heavily on individual quality.

With De Bruyne as the central orchestrator and wingers tasked with stretching the play, the team is currently in a transitional phase between generations. Their attacking output relies heavily on De Bruyne's visionary passing and Doku's ability to force 1v1 breakthroughs down the flanks.

Defensive counter-attacking approach with an over-reliance on Mohamed Salah. The overall tactical framework is built around Salah: the midfield and defensive lines prioritize disruption and defensive solidity, and upon regaining possession, the team immediately looks to transition quickly to Salah on the right flank.

A steel-hard defensive line paired with a lethal two-striker partnership. Recognized as Asia's most physically robust side, they boast an exceptionally solid defensive structure. In transition, they rely on the seamless chemistry of frontline predators such as Mehdi Taremi and Sardar Azmoun to punish opponents on the counter.

An open, end-to-end style characterized by the classic English direct approach. The system prioritizes physical duels and aerial dominance (exemplified by Wood), employing a straightforward, high-tempo tactical framework. Defensively, the team relies on numerical superiority and compact blocking to stifle opposition attacks.

Tiki-Taka 2.0 with explosive wing play. Building on the traditional possession framework, this approach now integrates a potent vertical threat, leveraging Lamine Yamal and Nico Williams on the flanks to create 1v1 isolation opportunities.

A "Bielsa-style" high-intensity pressing system featuring man-to-man marking across the entire pitch. This physically demanding approach emphasizes relentless, full-field pressure, with an immediate mandate to transition at maximum speed and deliver the ball into the penalty area the moment possession is won.

They employ a high defensive line combined with a possession-based, technical passing game. They are willing to implement an offside trap and apply intense high pressing even against top European sides. While their players exhibit fine technical skills on the ball, the space behind their defensive line remains vulnerable to being exploited.

Fearless against top-tier opposition, they employ a dynamic attacking style. Despite making their tournament debut, they do not adopt a conservative approach; their players possess exceptional technical ability on the ball and favor intricate short-passing combinations to penetrate defenses in tight spaces.

Pragmatism with Mbappé as the accelerant. Deschamps does not prioritize possession; the midfield is built on suffocating pressure and aggressive interceptions, while the attack leverages Mbappé's unstoppable pace to deliver a level-of-play mismatch.

Ødegaard orchestrates the build-up, while Haaland delivers the finish. The tactical intent is crystal clear: Ødegaard and his midfield partners will dictate the tempo and unlock defenses, channeling precise service to the "Demon" up front, Haaland.

A hybrid of Eastern and Western football philosophies, anchored by a formidable central spine. The team exhibits European-level tactical discipline, with center-backs and defensive midfielders possessing exceptional physical dueling capabilities, while the wide players boast explosive pace.

A compact defensive block paired with emotional, high-intensity football. After a long absence from the World Cup, they will deploy the most pragmatic five-back system for an underdog side, relying on sheer resilience and sporadic counter-attacks to stay competitive.

Maximum midfield dominance with intricate short-passing combinations. Rather than relying on outright pace, the side employs a technically gifted midfield core—featuring players like Mac Allister and Enzo—to dictate tempo, lull opponents into a false sense of security, and create decisive moments for the final blow.

The Ralf Rangnick-influenced Red Bull philosophy: suffocating pressing. One of the most aggressive high-pressing systems in Europe, placing paramount emphasis on reaction speed and vertical passing during the critical seconds of transition.

North African technical style with inverted wingers. The players possess exceptional dribbling and close-control skills, preferring to exploit space on the flanks through individual brilliance before cutting inside to shoot or deliver passes.

A counter-attacking dark horse that leverages wing-back surges. Building on their successful template at the Asian Cup, they drop into defensive shape with exceptional speed. In transition, they exploit the pace of their wing-backs and front three to create numerical overloads in the attacking third.

The attacking phase is a work of art, characterized by fluid ball retention. The squad boasts a formidable depth in its attacking line, with a tactical approach centered on dominating possession. Players such as Bernardo Silva, Bruno Fernandes, and Rafael Leão operate with positional fluidity, constantly interchanging roles to disrupt defensive structures.

Left-wing corridor and set-piece threat: The attack is heavily focused on the left flank through Luis Díaz, while set pieces taken by players such as James Rodríguez serve as a key weapon to break deadlocks.

Physical dominance combined with direct, vertical attacks. The squad boasts exceptional athletic profiles and explosive power, employing a rugged, high-intensity tactical approach. Once granted space on the counter-attack, they pose a formidable threat.

Eastern European discipline with a focal-point attacking approach. One of the most defensively solid sides in the Asian zone, they exhibit strong tactical execution. In attack, they rely on physically imposing forwards such as Shomurodov to serve as the central pivot.

Star-studded yet cautious in progression. Despite boasting elite talents such as Bellingham, Foden, and Saka in the final third, the overall tactical approach remains conservative, prioritizing the stability of the defensive shape.

A midfield iron triangle and masters of tempo control. Even as their core players age, they persist in leveraging the midfield's superior possession and ball-retention capabilities to drag the game into their preferred slow-paced rhythm.

Individual brilliance and chaos specialists. The squad boasts high-impact, individually gifted players such as Mohammed Kudus. They thrive on applying intense high pressing to disrupt the opponent's structure, deliberately creating chaotic situations in which they can exploit openings.

A true dark horse at the Copa América, this side employs a highly mobile defensive block. Their defensive structure is exceptionally compact, underpinned by players with outstanding work rate and stamina. They thrive on winning the ball in the middle and defensive thirds, then immediately launching rapid counterattacks through crisp, short-passing combinations.
